annotatedSteps.description: Identifying the colour coding of live and neutral wires
annotatedSteps.studentWork: (a) Live wire — red insulation; neutral wire — black insulation.
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Correct colour coding identified for both line wires.

annotatedSteps.description: Calculation of the current drawn by the 1 kW electric iron
Specifying the standard domestic circuit current rating
annotatedSteps.studentWork: So the current rating of the circuit should be 4.54 A.
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: × Domestic circuits come in standard ratings of 5 A and 15 A. Since the appliance draws 4.54 A, a 5 A circuit rating is required.
annotatedSteps.correctedWorking: Since current drawn is 4.54 A, a standard 5 A circuit rating must be used.

annotatedSteps.description: Explaining the function of the earth wire
annotatedSteps.studentWork: (c)(i) The earth wire provides a low-resistance conducting path to the earth,

annotatedSteps.description: Stating the advantage/safety role of the earth wire in appliances with metallic bodies
annotatedSteps.studentWork: so any current leaking to the metal body of the iron flows to the earth and the body stays at earth potential. Thus the user does not get an electric shock.
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Clear and accurate explanation of safety against electric shock.

teacherNote: Marked against: (a) Correct colours of insulation: Live wire is red and neutral wire is black (1); (b) Formula and calculation of electric current drawn: I = P/V = 1000/220 = 4.54 A (or 4.5 A) (0.5); (b) Required standard circuit rating: 5 A (0.5); (c)(i) Function of earth wire: Provides a low-resistance conducting path for electric current to the ground (1); (c)(i) Advantage in electric iron: Prevents severe electric shock to the user by keeping the metallic body at zero/earth potential in case of leakage (1). Excellent conceptual clarity on domestic wire colours and earthing function. Remember that in domestic supply systems, circuits are provided in standard ratings (5 A and 15 A), so a 4.54 A current requires a 5 A circuit rating.
